expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: Diagnoses root cause: 'Your broker has no committed position for your consumer, so every restart looks like a brand-new consumer and it falls back to the "start from" default (earliest / queue head)' and gives per-broker minimal fixes, e.g. 'enable.auto.commit=false but you never call commitSync()/commitAsync() after processing', 'delete after processing or extend the visibility timeout'.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: A runnable command with expected output exists mid-answer ('kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group <gid>: if CURRENT-OFFSET is - or far behind LOG-END-OFFSET, commits aren't landing'), but the answer ends with 'Tell me which broker and I'll point at the exact config lines.' — a question, so it does not end with a runnable checkpoint.

expectations.text: B3: Explains committing consumer offsets and resuming from the committed offset
expectations.evidence: Explains commit/resume mechanics: 'a new group has no committed offset, so auto.offset.reset (often earliest) applies', 'Commits fail silently during rebalances; check the CommitFailedException path', and 'is the offset/ack actually being persisted after successful processing'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: SHELL COMMANDS RUN (1): 'ls -la'; OTHER TOOL CALLS: glob only; FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0); no install commands and nothing written outside the workspace.
